stories.headline: Election Commision keeps RTI applicant waiting for reply
stories.title: Election Commision keeps RTI applicant waiting for reply
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: EC is yet to respond to an RTI application seeking details of steps taken to address grievances raised by two ECs and copies of files, including notings, related to the issue, despite the 30-day statutory time-limit for giving a reply lapsing, said applicant Commodore Lokesh K Batra (retd) Tuesday.

The application was filed on Sept 25 but the RTI status on EC’s website shows “32 day” and still “in-progress”, Batra said, asking “why EC is maintaining a deafening silence” and “what is EC hiding?” The activist sought copies of the complete set of records of issues and grievances raised by ECs SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
On Sept 24, in a separate RTI to cabinet secretariat, Batra sought copies of the EC’s communications, details of steps taken and file notings.
He received a response on Oct 19, and documents and file notings on Oct 22.

stories.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for US after election defeat and passport order
stories.title: Flavio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for US after election defeat and passport order
stories.summary: The senator’s departure comes amid a money laundering probe and uncertainty over how he travelled abroad despite a Supreme Court deadline
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election and refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports, two sources said.
The US Embassy in Brazil did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Bolsonaro’s lawyer also did not respond.
It was not immediately clear where Bolsonaro was heading, when he would arrive or whether he would seek asylum.
US President Donald Trump’s administration has previously alleged that Flavio’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.
Flavio’s departure for the United States threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to return them to power.
Reuters reported ahead of Sunday’s election that the US State Department had campaigned to restore them to office.
Bolsonaro was favoured to win Sunday’s presidential election but suffered a shock defeat to leftist Lula.
On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing.
That deadline has now passed, and his documents have been cancelled, two other sources said.
It was unclear whether he could enter the United States with his passports cancelled.

opening: Mumbai: India's capital market regulator is taking a relook at the onerous extra disclosure rules for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is expected to release a consultation paper for feedback on possible relaxation of the regulations that require FPIs above a certain asset size or having concentrated equity exposure to a company or a corporate group to share granular details of investors in the funds." Sebi had sounded out some of the market participants and fund custodians.
body: What we understand is that it wants to rationalise the rules so that the twin objective, to enhance transparency and prevent circumvention of regulations by FPIs without causing any collateral damage like driving a fund to sell shares to lower its holding, is met," a person familiar with the discussions told ET.

One of the suggestions includes fixing a low threshold equity holding in a company below which an FPI would not have to give details of their investors even if the fund is focused on one or two firms or group.
UBO Details.

Also, it has been proposed that FPI with concentrated investments in professionally-run companies with no identifiable promoters and public sector undertakings should be exempted from additional disclosure requirements.
The Sebi spokesperson did not comment on the matter.

Under the additional disclosure regulations, which came in the wake of US firm Hindenburg Research's allegations against the Adani Group, an FPI is required to reveal the ultimate beneficial owners, down to the last natural persons, of all investors in the fund if it crosses either of the following thresholds: (1) if more than 50% of the India equity assets under management is in a company or a single corporate group; (2) if a fund's AUM in Indian equities is ₹50,000 crore or more.

The disclosure rule also kicks in if multiple FPIs having common ownership or control together breach the limits." While Sebi has till now exempted certain FPIs like sovereign funds, public retail funds, and university funds, but those who want to focus on a few stocks as per their strategy are caught in the detailed disclosure rule.

Some rationalisation, particularly, deciding an FPI's maximum holding in a company under which the fund could be spared from additional disclosures." Among other things, the rules are aimed at preventing violation of minimum public shareholding regulation by restraining promoters or connected entities from using FPIs to mask concentrated holdings; sidestepping takeover norms; and blocking circumvention of Press Note 3 which requires government approval for investments from land-bordering countries.

sentences.text: Under the additional disclosure regulations, which came in the wake of US firm Hindenburg Research's allegations against the Adani Group, an FPI is required to reveal the ultimate beneficial owners, down to the last natural persons, of all investors in the fund if it crosses either of the following thresholds: (1) if more than 50% of the India equity assets under management is in a company or a single corporate group; (2) if a fund's AUM in Indian equities is ₹50,000 crore or more.

Among other things, the rules are aimed at preventing violation of minimum public shareholding regulation by restraining promoters or connected entities from using FPIs to mask concentrated holdings; sidestepping takeover norms; and blocking circumvention of Press Note 3 which requires government approval for investments from land-bordering countries.
